business_problem: Forbes needed to replace an aging on-premises CMS database environment that slowed contributors and developers, required hands-on infrastructure work, and made it harder to add new tools and capabilities for its digital publishing business.
solution_summary: Forbes modernized the CMS and developer environment behind its digital publishing business on MongoDB Atlas so contributors and engineers could move faster than an aging on-premises platform allowed. Atlas became the managed operational database for the content management system that publishes to Forbes.com, replacing hands-on work around disk changes, security patching, compliance, and disaster recovery. MongoDB Professional Services helped the team optimize early queries and performance, while developers used MongoDB University to transfer familiar SQL skills into the new document model. Atlas's flexible structures, auto-scaling storage, and easy local/cloud installation let Forbes orchestrate the frontend API and database together, speed provisioning and recovery, and cut average build times from 25 minutes to nine minutes while improving the reader experience.

The Atlas-backed frontend API then serves pages to Forbes.com, while auto-scaling, managed recovery, and provisioning workflows help developers release and operate the platform faster.
